source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Use diluted potassium chloride by controlled IV infusion according to protocol rather than direct administration of the concentrate.","B":"Give the concentrated potassium chloride directly when symptoms are severe because rapid replacement is safer than waiting for dilution.","C":"Give concentrated potassium chloride through a central line without dilution because central access removes the cardiac risk of direct dosing.","D":"Give concentrated potassium chloride directly after a normal ECG because a normal tracing makes the undiluted route acceptable."}}
source_row.rationale: Current labeling requires concentrated potassium chloride to be diluted before intravenous administration and identifies direct administration of the concentrate as potentially fatal. Option A is correct because it uses dilution and controlled infusion. Options B and D incorrectly endorse direct concentrated administration. Option C incorrectly assumes central access removes the danger of undiluted potassium.
source_row.source_detail: DailyMed Potassium Chloride for Injection Concentrate, USP — Boxed Warning and Dosage and Administration: FOR IV INFUSION ONLY AFTER DILUTION; direct/undiluted administration may be instantaneously fatal and can cause fatal arrhythmia or cardiac arrest. Hospira FDA label updated 2026-07-01; current DailyMed version published 2026-07-06 and live-rechecked 2026-08-15.
